strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: The Rust runtime revalidates WriteWorkspace permission at the final proposal.apply mutation authority.
Single-file apply, multi-file transaction apply, and transaction recovery apply deny before writing when the source run mode lacks WriteWorkspace.
Apply-time permission decisions are recorded as bounded PermissionChecked and PermissionDenied evidence without raw file content or paths outside existing workspace-relative summaries.
Headless callers receive deterministic runtime-owned admission or denial at the moment of workspace mutation.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances runtime_permission_enforcement with supporting controlled_workspace_tools, persistent_structured_ledger, and headless_autonomous_development.
answers.new_capability: proposal.apply can mutate only after apply-time WriteWorkspace permission revalidation succeeds.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Proposal-generation permission checks happen before final apply and cannot protect stale approved proposal evidence at mutation time.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: The most sensitive workspace mutation RPC would remain guarded by approval and preflight gates but not by a final runtime mode-policy decision.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M13.3 revalidated provider retry provenance, M14.1 added transaction apply, and M14.2 added recovery apply; M15.1 hardens permission admission for all apply writes.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing proposal.apply RPC is hardened.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase records bounded permission evidence and apply result checks tied to actual admission behavior.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Denied, missing, malformed, or unknown WriteWorkspace permission fails closed before apply writes or consumes authorization.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Autonomous controllers can rely on Rust-owned permission enforcement at the final workspace side-effect boundary.
answers.milestone_progress: Starts M15 with concrete permission hardening on Brownie's highest-impact mutation authority.
